    Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel to India next week for a visit focused on deepening cooperation in energy and spurring investment and economic opportunities.
    Book Says Russian Diesel Won’t Offset Price Surge
    Kevin Book, ClearView Energy Partners managing director, says additional Russian diesel is unlikely to offset the roughly 70% run-up in diesel prices, though he estimates increased volumes could provide roughly 5 to 20 cents a gallon in relief by the end of the fourth quarter. Book also warns that further escalation in the Middle East could put more critical Saudi energy infrastructure at risk, potentially creating a much larger disruption to oil markets. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
    Trump Calls on Hochul to Remove James From Cornell Investigation
    President Donald Trump called on New York’s governor to remove state Attorney General Letitia James from the investigation into an alleged rape at Cornell University, injecting himself into a case that has drawn national attention.
    Rep. Letlow Says Farmers Need Relief From Diesel Prices
    Rep. Julia Letlow (R-LA), Republican Nominee for the US Senate from Louisiana, says high diesel prices are putting pressure on farmers during harvest season, with some producers talking about going under. Rep. Letlow says she appreciates the Trump administration looking at every avenue possible to bring prices down, acknowledging that some of those solutions have been controversial. Rep. Lutlow also discusses her Know Your Risk Act, which would direct the government to develop a common breast cancer risk assessment tool to help individuals better understand their risk. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
    Carney Heads to Alberta Days Before Canada Separation Vote
    Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is heading to Alberta days before residents of the oil-rich province head to the polls to vote on a referendum to remain in Canada or seek independence.
    US to Use Cold War-Era Law to Expand Delek Refinery in Texas
    Vice President JD Vance announced Trump administration plans to work with Delek US Holdings Inc. to expand a refinery in Texas, the latest energy investment highlighted as a way to lower fuel prices before the November midterm elections.
    Russia Arrests Japanese Reporter for Espionage as Spat Grows
    Russian authorities said they’d detained a Japanese journalist on suspicion of espionage, with a court ruling that he be held in custody for two months, the Federal Security Service (FSB) said in a statement on its website.
    Guilfoyle Ousted as US Ambassador to Greece Amid Conduct Probe
    President Donald Trump ousted his US Ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, following allegations of unethical conduct.
    Duterte Impeachment Trial to Focus on Hidden Wealth Charge
    Philippine prosecutors in a surprise move on Tuesday dropped most of the impeachment charges against Vice President Sara Duterte, opting to zero in on her alleged hidden wealth as the sole ground to oust and disqualify her from public office.

    The Gulf has entered a new era of instability. If its leaders think they can rely on old alliances, they are wrong | Nesrine Malik
    The latest attack by Houthi rebels on Saudi Arabia may prove to be more calamitous for the region than the world imagines On Saturday, Houthi rebels launched a shocking and deadly attack on Saudi Arabia’s capital city, Riyadh. At the time of writing, the missile strike on King Khalid international airport has killed at least 13 people and left 300 injured, marking a significant turn in a regional conflagration that is only getting more intense. It was the single most deadly attack on any Gulf country since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran in February. In Saudi Arabia, a country that is unaccustomed to such fatalities, the death toll is bewilderingly high and likely to prompt a bloody response.
